In this address, Kennedy explicitly criticized Ronald Reagan—then the Republican presidential nominee and a former Hollywood actor (who would become the 40th U.S. president)—and implicitly rebuked incumbent President Jimmy Carter (to whom Kennedy had conceded the Democratic nomination the night before) for his moderate stances. The speech defended liberal values, advocated for national healthcare, and took aim at both candidates in the 1980 presidential race.
